extracted.intended_audience: IB Mathematics students and teachers (Analysis and Approaches) preparing/submitting the mathematical exploration (internal assessment)
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric and guidance for assessing the IB mathematics exploration (internal assessment) for SL and HL in the Analysis and Approaches course. Specifies the five assessment criteria, achievement levels, and explanatory guidance for students and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment structure and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exploration is assessed against five criteria (A–E). The final mark is the sum of scores for each criterion. Maximum possible final mark is 20. Students will not receive a grade for the mathematics course if they have not submitted an exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explorations are internally assessed by the teacher and externally moderated by the IB. Teachers should ensure submission; absence of an exploration means no course grade. Scores for each criterion are summed to produce the exploration mark (out of 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the organization and coherence of the exploration. Achievement levels 0–4: from 'does not reach standard' to 'coherent, well organized, and concise.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A coherent exploration is logically developed, easy to follow and meets its aim (introduction, body, conclusion, and linking of parts). A well-organized exploration includes an introduction, aim, and conclusion. Relevant graphs, tables and diagrams should accompany the work in the appropriate place and not be attached as appendices; appendices are for large data sets or additional material. A concise exploration avoids irrelevant or unnecessary repetitive calculations, graphs or descriptions. Use of technology is encouraged where appropriate but analytic approaches are not penalized. Repetitive calculations are not condoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B: Mathematical communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the extent to which the student uses appropriate mathematical language, defines terms and variables, uses multiple representations, and uses deductive method/proofs where appropriate. Achievement levels 0–4 from 'does not reach standard' to 'relevant, appropriate and consistent throughout.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should use appropriate mathematical language (notation, symbols, terminology). Calculator/computer notation is acceptable only if software-generated; otherwise standard mathematical notation is expected. Key terms and variables should be defined where required. Students should use multiple forms of representation (formulae, diagrams, tables, charts, graphs, models) as appropriate. Deductive methods and logically set out proofs are expected where appropriate. Examples: level 1 may include unlabeled graphs or consistent use of computer notation with no other correct communication; level 4 can be achieved using only one form of representation if appropriate. Minor errors that do not impair clear communication should not be penalized at level 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion C: Personal engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the extent to which the student engages with the topic by exploring the mathematics and 'making it their own.' Achievement levels 0–3 from 'does not reach standard' to 'evidence of outstanding personal engagement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal engagement is not a measure of effort; it is shown by independent or creative thinking, presenting ideas in the student's own way, exploring from different perspectives, making and testing predictions, etc. Engagement must be evident in the student's work (teacher testimony is insufficient). Textbook-style reproductions without the student's perspective are unlikely to achieve higher levels. 'Significant' engagement appears on a few occasions and drives the exploration forward; 'outstanding' engagement is numerous, high-quality instances that drive the exploration creatively and leave an impression of full understanding of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D: Reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses how the student reviews, analyses and evaluates the exploration. Achievement levels 0–3 from 'does not reach standard' to 'substantial evidence of critical reflection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection can occur throughout the exploration or in the conclusion. Simple description of results is limited reflection; higher levels require further consideration. Meaningful reflection includes linking to the aims, commenting on what was learned, considering limitations, or comparing different mathematical approaches. Critical reflection is deeply insightful (discussing 'what next', implications of results, strengths/weaknesses of approaches, different perspectives) and should develop the exploration. To reach the highest level, critical reflection should be present throughout or be high-quality if only in the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E: Use of mathematics — SL
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses to what extent students use mathematics relevant to the exploration at SL. Achievement levels 0–6 describe increasing correctness and depth from 'does not reach standard' to 'the mathematics explored is correct. Thorough knowledge and understanding are demonstrated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant mathematics supports the development of the exploration toward its aim. 'Relevant' excludes overly complicated mathematics used without need. Work should be commensurate with the level of the course and not be completely based on prior learning only; mathematics should be part of the syllabus or at a similar level. 'Demonstrate' means make clear by reasoning or evidence; obtaining correct answers alone is insufficient to show understanding. Occasional minor errors that do not detract from flow are acceptable. Use of technology is encouraged but understanding must be demonstrated (e.g., mere substitution into a formula is not sufficient). Students are advised to do a few things well rather than many things poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E: Use of mathematics — HL
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses to what extent students use relevant mathematics in the exploration at HL. Achievement levels 0–6 from 'does not reach standard' to 'precise mathematics demonstrating sophistication and rigour; thorough knowledge and understanding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should use mathematics commensurate with HL (or at similar/slightly beyond level). Demonstration of understanding (reasoning, evidence, examples) is required — correct answers alone are insufficient. Lines of reasoning must be shown to justify steps. 'Relevant' mathematics supports the aim; avoid unnecessarily complicated methods. Occasional minor errors are acceptable if they do not detract. 'Precision' implies error-free mathematics and appropriate accuracy. 'Sophistication' means use of challenging concepts, multiple perspectives, and linking areas of mathematics (may include HL syllabus content or SL content used in complex ways). 'Rigour' involves clarity of logic and justification/proofs for mathematical claims. Use of technology is allowed but does not replace demonstrated understanding. As for SL, doing a few things well is preferable.
